title: Incident-bot: post failover state transitions to #incidents + /failover status commands
author: Owen Phillips
body:
Summary: This PR adds automated Slack notifications to #incidents when the failover orchestrator changes state (monitor-only -> canary -> progressive -> full, plus rollback/hold-down/abort) and introduces a small set of incident-bot commands to query current failover mode per region/route/model with links to the dashboards + runbook.

Context: Regional failover automation upgrade requires an auditable and low-friction way for on-call to understand what automation is doing in real time. During recent regional degradation threads, we were manually pasting screenshots/links and re-checking routing state in multiple places. This adds a single source of truth message format and makes the state queryable directly in Slack.

What’s included (high level): 1) Event ingestion: incident-bot subscribes to Failover Orchestrator events over NATS (topic: failover.state.v1) and normalizes them into a message envelope with correlation IDs and actor. 2) #incidents notifications: on state transitions, bot posts a structured message with: previous_state -> new_state, region, scope (tier/route/model), reason (trigger summary), safe-to-failover checks (capacity/dependency), and explicit runbook + dashboard links. 3) Commands: /failover status [--region us-east-1] [--route /v1/chat/completions] [--model redwood/llama-3.1-70b] returns current mode, last transition time, hold-down timer, and most recent decision record link. /failover recent [--region ...] returns last N transitions. /failover help includes examples and escalation guidance. 4) Permissions and safety: commands require membership in oncall-failover-control (read-only for status/recent; no mutate actions in this PR). The event handler rate-limits posts and dedupes repeated events (same transition id) to avoid spam. 5) Links: dashboards and runbook links are standardized and built from config: - Runbook: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ONCALL/Automated+Region+Failover+Runbook - Dashboard (health overview): https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/failover-region-health - Dashboard (state machine/audit): https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/failover-state-audit

Message format (example): "Failover state change: us-east-1 MONITOR_ONLY → CANARY (5%) | scope=tier:hosted_free, route:/v1/chat/completions, model:redwood/mixtral-8x7b | reason=p95_latency_burn(10m)=3.2x + 5xx(5m)=1.8% | safe-to-failover=PASS (capacity_headroom=27%, deps=OK) | decision=FO-DEC-20250412-1931 | dashboards: [health] [audit] | runbook".

Implementation details: - New module failover_events/consumer.ts handles NATS subscription, schema validation (zod), dedupe cache (LRU w/ 15m TTL), and mapping to Slack blocks. - Slack posting uses existing incident-bot queue + retry logic; added a separate "failover" channel route that always posts to #incidents and also threads into an existing incident if an incident channel is active and correlation_id matches (best-effort). - Decision record links: we build a URL from orchestrator decision_id and region, e.g. https://console.redwoodinference.com/admin/failover/decisions/FO-DEC-... (this is internal-only; link behind SSO). - Config: added FAILOVER_ORCH_NATS_URL, FAILOVER_EVENTS_TOPIC (default failover.state.v1), FAILOVER_DASHBOARD_URL_* in env schema; also added a feature flag INCIDENT_BOT_FAILOVER_POSTING=on|off|dry-run (default dry-run in prod). - Tests: unit tests cover schema validation, dedupe behavior, and Slack block rendering. Added an integration-ish test using a mocked NATS client to ensure subscription + handler wiring.

Rollout plan: - Staging: enable INCIDENT_BOT_FAILOVER_POSTING=on and validate message volume during staging game day. - Prod: ship with dry-run for 48h; validate metrics (events received, posts attempted, dedupe hits). Then flip to on during a staffed window (SRE + Platform on-call) per release gating.

Observability: - Metrics: incident_bot_failover_events_received_total, incident_bot_failover_posts_sent_total, incident_bot_failover_posts_deduped_total, incident_bot_failover_posts_failed_total, and command latency histograms. - Logs include transition_id, decision_id, and Slack message timestamp for audit.

Out of scope: - No write/override commands (enable/disable/rollback) in Slack; this PR is read-only plus notifications. - No changes to orchestrator decisioning; only consuming its emitted events.

Testing: - yarn test (unit) - yarn lint - local run with NATS dev container; published sample events and verified Slack formatting in #incidents-staging.

Checklist: - [x] Added RBAC gate for commands - [x] Added rate limiting + dedupe - [x] Added metrics + alertable failure signal (posts_failed) - [x] Added docs in /docs/commands.md - [x] Verified dry-run mode in prod config

References: Linear ENG-2848; aligns with runbook updates owned by Tomáš and dashboards spec owned by Aisha/Sergio.
commits: feat(failover): subscribe to failover.state.v1 and validate event schema
feat(slack): render failover transition message blocks + standardized links
chore(rbac): gate failover commands behind oncall-failover-control
test: add unit tests for dedupe + block rendering; mock NATS client
docs: document commands and dry-run rollout instructions
checks: CI / unit tests: pass (rerun required after initial flaky timeout in mocked NATS test)
conversation:
Rafael Mendes (review): Can we ensure we don’t spam #incidents during flappy transitions? I want a hard dedupe keyed on transition_id and also a minimum interval per region.

Owen Phillips (author): Added LRU dedupe keyed on transition_id (15m) and a per-region post cooldown (60s) that only applies to repeated identical state pairs; true transitions still post. Also added a metric for deduped posts.

Aisha Bello (review): Please include direct links to the failover SLO burn dashboard, not just the state/audit dashboard. That’s what on-call will check first.

Owen Phillips (author): Added FAILOVER_DASHBOARD_URL_HEALTH + FAILOVER_DASHBOARD_URL_SLO_BURN and included both in the message. Kept state/audit as third link.

Tomáš Novák (review): Runbook link should go to the automated failover runbook page (not the parent space). Also can we add a one-liner in the message about manual override location?

Owen Phillips (author): Updated runbook URL to the specific page and added: "Manual override: see Runbook > 'Override + rollback'" in the message footer.

Connor O'Brien (review): For rollout safety, default prod should be dry-run. Also add a config validation failure if posting is enabled but #incidents channel id is missing.

Owen Phillips (author): Done. Prod defaults to dry-run; env schema now requires INCIDENTS_CHANNEL_ID when posting=on.

Final approvals: Rafael Mendes (approved), Aisha Bello (approved), Tomáš Novák (approved), Connor O'Brien (approved).
release_notes: Internal: incident-bot now posts automated failover state transitions to #incidents and supports /failover status queries (read-only), improving visibility during regional degradation and controlled failover tests.
